- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model forecasts often overshoot and fail to correct — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day post-spike.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model forecasts tend to underestimate — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean to offset bearish bias.  
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model forecasts often lag the true outcome — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with event-driven volatility.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.67) and supply net is negative, model forecasts are overly optimistic — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to reflect muted sentiment.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), adjust forecast to flatten slope toward mid-range historical mean.
